note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: KV-cache bottleneck and shallow-layer gap -> redundancy observations -> SpindleKV design -> evaluation

nodes.name: KV cache is a deployment bottleneck
nodes.description: KV cache memory grows proportionally with context length and can exceed the memory occupied by the model parameters, becoming a bottleneck for LLM deployment.

nodes.name: Prior reduction works better in deep layers
nodes.description: Token eviction, merging and quantization are generally more effective for deeper layers than shallower ones, so shallow-layer KV reduction has been largely overlooked.

nodes.name: Deep-layer attention is sparse
nodes.description: As layer depth increases, more tokens receive low accumulated attention scores and attention concentrates on a few tokens, supporting token eviction in deep layers.

nodes.name: Shallow-layer KV constituents are highly similar
nodes.description: In shallow layers many tokens receive high attention yet their KV constituent components are highly similar (high cosine similarity), indicating inner-token compositional redundancy beyond inter-token redundancy.

nodes.name: GQA hinders attention-score eviction
nodes.description: Attention-score-based eviction such as PyramidInfer and PyramidKV integrates poorly with GQA because eviction must be decided for an entire group of Q heads rather than per head, and KV heads in GQA hold higher information density.

nodes.name: SpindleKV balances shallow and deep layers
nodes.description: SpindleKV combines attention-weight-based token eviction for deep layers with a learned codebook-based replacement for shallow layers, and addresses the GQA dilemma.

nodes.name: Eviction with linear layer allocation
nodes.description: Deep-layer eviction follows PyramidKV's linear interpolation of per-layer reserve ratios and SnapKV's observation window, using accumulated attention scores as token importance.

nodes.name: Codebook replacement
nodes.description: In prefill, SpindleKV builds K and V codebooks greedily so every token has a codebook entry with cosine similarity above a threshold, storing only indices and per-vector magnitudes.

nodes.name: Magnitude reconstruction
nodes.description: Because cosine similarity captures direction but not magnitude, SpindleKV records each vector's magnitude and rescales after codebook lookup, which effectively preserves model capability with slight memory cost.

nodes.name: GQA ablation
nodes.description: On LLaMA3-8b-instruct, SpindleKV's GQA handling outperforms the PyramidInfer-style averaged-attention eviction approach, addressing the GQA dilemma.

nodes.name: Codebook alone halves the cache losslessly
nodes.description: With eviction removed, codebook replacement on LLaMA2-7b-chat compresses half the KV cache without accuracy impact and retains most capability at 30% KV cache.

nodes.name: LongBench results
nodes.description: On LongBench with LLaMA2-7b, LLaMA3-8b and Mistral-7b, SpindleKV achieves higher reduction at comparable performance than PyramidInfer and PyramidKV, in some settings reducing KV cache size 50% without performance loss, and beats PyramidKV on 13 Mistral datasets.

nodes.name: Needle-in-a-Haystack results
nodes.description: With only 15% KV cache reserved, SpindleKV maintains retrieval recall significantly better than PyramidInfer and PyramidKV.

isolated_nodes.name: Needed model setup
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments use LLaMA2-7b-chat (MHA), LLaMA3-8b-instruct and Mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2 (GQA, 8 KV heads, 4 Q heads per KV head) on LongBench's 16 subsets and Needle-in-a-Haystack.

isolated_nodes.name: Merging and RoPE overhead
isolated_nodes.description: The codebook is built on pre-RoPE keys so RoPE must be re-applied after reconstruction, which adds no substantial time overhead.

structural_reasoning: Motivation and observations on layer-wise redundancy lead to the hybrid design; each design component is validated by ablations and benchmarks.
